newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKETS OUTLOOK - Q3 GDP, payrolls loom.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKETS OUTLOOK - Q3 GDP, payrolls loom.

text.p: Fresh evidence of a slowdown in U.S. economic growth and steady wage costs should stoke credit markets next week at least until Friday's overshadowing U.S. payrolls report, analysts said on Friday.

The release of the third quarter employment cost index (ECI) and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) on Tuesday, October 29, and Wednesday, October 30, respectively, should support, if not bolster, current debt market levels, economists said.

But Friday, November 1's double bill of October U.S. payrolls and the October National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index could create some volatility if the data differ significantly from market consensus.

"Certainly anything over 250,000 (October payrolls) will make people nervous. Anything over 300,000 is just going to knock the stuffing out of the market," said John Canavan, bond market analyst at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
A Reuter poll shows economists on average forecast a 212,000 rise in October payrolls compared to a 40,000 drop in September. The data is set for release at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

"We should see a fair number of payrolls back on the service side as stores look to staff back up for Christmas," said Richard Koss, economist at MFR Inc, who sees a relatively high 275,000 rise in October payrolls.
"But it's not enough to get the Federal Reserve to tighten (key short-term interest rates) soon," he added.

Cheryl Katz, senior economist at Merrill Lynch, estimated a 150,000 gain in October payrolls, stating a more moderate economic growth outlook than most economic pundits as reason for the relatively low forecast.
Katz cautioned an increase in the U.S. minimum wage, which took effect in October, would account for roughly half the gains expected in the key average hourly earnings component.
She estimated a 0.4 percent rise in October and said a gain over 0.6 percent would hurt the bond market.
On average, third quarter GDP, scheduled for a 0830 EST/1330 GMT release, is expected to grow a subdued 1.8 percent in comparison to a 4.7 percent jump in the second quarter.
Analysts said a large chunk of third-quarter growth should be attributed to a sharp pick-up in inventory building.
"If you exclude inventories, final sales rose at only a 0.3 percent rate," Katz forecasted.
Tuesday's third quarter ECI index is seen growing 0.8 percent compared to the prior quarter. Growth in the second quarter was 0.7 percent from the first.
Following payrolls on Friday will be the NAPM index at 1000 EST/1500 GMT. The Reuter poll shows an expected reading of 51.0 for October, compared to September's 51.7 figure.
The forecast hovers just above the break-even level of 50.0, which suggests manufacturing activity remains mediocre, economists said.

A slew of other, secondary data litters next week's calendar. Other data releases include: October consumer confidence index on Monday, September new homes sales on Tuesday, September personal income and consumption along with the October Chicago Purchasing Managers index on Thursday, and September factory orders and leading indicators on Friday.
Also, on Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury will announce the size and timing of its upcoming three- and 10-year note and 30-year bond auctions.
